To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed time delay and image separation in gravitational lens systems might not uniquely determine either the concentration or the extent of the mass distribution of the lens galaxy, which is a consequence of the intrinsic degeneracy in the lens model.

(i) the observed time delays and image positions do not fully determine the mass distribution of the lens galaxy, even with very accurate measurements; (ii) a degeneracy between a Keplerian and a flat rotation curve exists, even when the cosmological parameters are fixed; (iii) the observed lens galaxy mass profile is consistent with a flat rotation curve; (iv) this degeneracy can be broken only if the cosmological parameters (Ω, Λ, H0) are allowed to vary

(i) the intrinsic time delay degeneracy is a real effect that is not due to the lens model, (ii) it is present in any lensing system, (iii) it is not removed by using the standard ΛCDMs values of H0 and Λ in the lens model, and (iv) it is not eliminated by using the best-fit values of H0, Λ, and other parameters in a strong lens system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can a degeneracy be found in strong lens models that exists rigourously?
the following questions: (1) How does the intrinsic degeneracy in lens mass models affect our ability to measure the Hubble constant from lensing time delays?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrinsic degeneracy is a fact, and it is not a problem.
the intrinsic degeneracy of strong gravitational lens time delay models is a serious obstacle in getting reliable values of H0 and Λ.
the intrinsic degeneracy in lens models is a reality and the degeneracy in H0 and Ω is not a mere artefact of the data analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed lensing time delay data are not sufficient to uniquely determine the lens galaxy mass profile.

, even in ΛCDM cosmological model, a simple lens system with a quadruple quasar images and a time delay can be fit with two different lens mass models, with a Keplerian mass distribution and a flat rotation curve mass distribution, both with the same H0, Λ, and Ω.
we find that the degeneracy in the strong lens mass model is intrinsic to the lensing problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lensing degeneracy is not a mere nuisance, but a serious problem.
the lens mass distribution can have very different mass distributions and the observed time delay and image positions cannot uniquely determine the lens mass distribution.
the degeneracy is a real and intrinsic feature of the lens system.
